Mr. ___ is an ___ year-old man with PMH significant for HTN,
HLD, presenting s/p syncope with concern for STEMI.
He reports that he was outside at a cookout tonight.

Prior to 
dinner he had a shot of vodka and also a glass of wine.

He then 
had a very large meal.

He was walking to the dessert table and 
was considering the fruit salad, when he decided he did not want 
dessert and put down his plate.
He then had LOC for < 1 sec.

He 
fell on his knees and also hit his elbow but had no head strike.

Preceding his syncope he felt hot, uncomfortable, thirsty, and 
bloated but not diaphoretic or nauseous.

He had no chest pain, 
palpitations, or preceding dyspnea.

He has had two very similar episodes in the past, both 
occurring after eating a large meal.
He is very active and exercises often.

He goes to the gym every 
other day and completes 20 minute workouts.

He also walks ___ 
miles a day.

He never has any chest discomfort during this 
activity.

He was told in the past that he had coronary artery 
disease after an abnormal pharmacologic stress test.
